title: DataAnnotations
description: DataAnnotations provide a built-in way to add validation rules directly to model classes using attributes. They are the simplest way to add validation in ASP.NET Core applications.

data.text: DataAnnotations are attributes in the System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations namespace. You apply them to model properties to declare rules such as required fields, string length limits, and range checks. ASP.NET Core automatically validates them during model binding.

data.title: Applying DataAnnotations
data.content: Add validation attributes to a Product model.

terms.definition: Ensures a property has a non-null value.
Specifies the maximum and optionally minimum length of a string.
Validates that a numeric value falls within a specified range.
Validates a value against a regex pattern.

data.title: Client-Side Validation
data.text: DataAnnotations work on the server by default. To enable client-side validation in MVC, include the necessary JavaScript and ensure jQuery Validation is loaded.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: DataAnnotations use attributes to declare validation rules
ASP.NET Core validates them automatically during model binding
ModelState.IsValid tells you whether validation passed
data.takeaway: DataAnnotations are the quickest way to add basic validation to your models.

data.title: Exercise: Validate a Registration Form
data.description: Apply DataAnnotations to a user registration model.
steps: Create a RegisterUserModel with Username, Email, Password, and ConfirmPassword
Apply Required, StringLength, EmailAddress, and Compare attributes
Create an API controller with a POST endpoint that accepts the model
Return a 400 response with validation errors if ModelState is invalid
Test with valid and invalid payloads
data.expectedOutcome: Invalid payloads return descriptive validation errors; valid payloads proceed normally.
